intro: The proprietor gestures at four shelves. The goods on them look identical: folders. He assures you they are not identical. He is right, which is the problem.

typeSigns.name: PROCEDURES
typeSigns.sign: Instructions the party reads when the situation matches. Cost nothing to carry. Cost everything to rely on.

typeSigns.name: SCOUTS
typeSigns.sign: They go ahead with their own supplies and come back with one sentence. The sentence is the product.

typeSigns.name: STANDING ORDERS
typeSigns.sign: Fire whether or not anyone remembers, believes, or objects. The wagon does not get a vote.

typeSigns.name: TRADE ROUTES
typeSigns.sign: Connections to somewhere else that has what you need. What the somewhere else needs from you is a separate question, and it is not on the sign.

proprietor.greeting: Buy anything. I don't check what's in them. Historically, neither do you.
proprietor.genericSale: Wrapped and loaded. No refunds. The refund policy is also in a folder.
proprietor.trapProcedureSale: A fine choice. Works four times out of five, and the fifth time is a long way from my stall.
proprietor.trapRouteChampionDead: The route works immediately. The discount was real. The wagon feels lighter, which you attribute to the savings.

championIntercept: {champion} reads the route's manifest at the perimeter, twice. "It works," they say. "So does a listening post." The route is quarantined, logged, and priced into the incident report they have already started writing.
